basics.description: SumOffice: Excel-compatible (SumSheet) and Word-compatible (SumDoc) editors for Nextcloud on one Ubuntu 24.04 LTS virtual machine. Files stay real .xlsx, .xlsm and .docx in your Nextcloud.

basics.name: vmName
basics.label: Virtual machine name
basics.toolTip: Name of the virtual machine; also used as the prefix of the network resources.

constraints.validationMessage: 3 to 42 characters: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens; starts with a letter, does not end with a hyphen.

basics.name: adminUsername
basics.label: Administrator user name
basics.toolTip: User name for SSH access to the virtual machine.

toolTip.sshPublicKey: SSH public key for the administrator.

elements.name: vmSize
elements.label: Size
elements.toolTip: 2 GB RAM for the server plus about 250 MB per open document. The editor images are x86-64.

elements.name: sshSourceAddressPrefix
elements.label: Allow SSH from
elements.toolTip: Source address prefix for port 22, e.g. 203.0.113.0/24, or * for any address. Ports 80 and 443 are open to everyone (the editors and the certificate check).

constraints.validationMessage: Enter * or an IPv4 address or CIDR range.

elements.name: nextcloudUrl
elements.label: Nextcloud address
elements.toolTip: The address your users open Nextcloud at. Only this Nextcloud may open files in the editors.

constraints.validationMessage: Scheme and host only, e.g. https://cloud.example.com (no path, no trailing slash).

elements.name: customDomain
elements.label: DNS name of your own (optional)
elements.toolTip: Leave empty to use the Azure DNS name of the VM's public IP address. If you enter a name, point its A or CNAME record at the VM after deployment; the certificate is issued once the record resolves.

constraints.validationMessage: A DNS name such as office.example.com, without https://.

options.text: The editors are free for evaluation; production use inside an organisation is licensed per application.
